name: Mate in one
goal: You can tell checkmate from check, and find a mate in one move when there is one.

intro.text: Checkmate ends the game: the king is in check and there is no way out. It cannot move to a safe square, the check cannot be blocked, and the checking piece cannot be taken. If even one of those ways is open, it is only check, so look at every check you have and test each one.

parts.title: Check or mate?
parts.keyIdea: Not every check is mate: test each check for an escape square, a block and a capture.
parts.text: From a game played on Lichess. Black's queen has just moved to c6. Your queen can give check in several ways, but only one of them is mate. For each check, ask where the king could go and whether Black could block or capture.

credit.authors: Lichess; the position is from a game played there

notes.text: Qf8 gives check along the back rank. The king cannot go to g8 or g7, because the queen covers both, and h7 is taken by its own pawn. Black's queen cannot block on g8 or take on f8, so it is mate. Compare Qc8+, which is only check: Black's queen simply takes yours.

parts.title: The queen and a helper
parts.keyIdea: The queen can mate right next to the king when another piece guards her.
parts.text: From a game played on Lichess. Black has just taken a pawn on c4. Your queen and your rook on g2 stand on the same file. Find the mate.

credit.authors: Lichess; the position is from a game played there

notes.text: The queen takes the g7 pawn and checks the king. The king cannot take her, because your rook on g2 guards g7, and it has nowhere to run: the queen covers g8 and h7. Checkmate.

parts.title: Check, block, mate
parts.keyIdea: A king boxed in by its own pawns can be mated along the back rank.
parts.text: From a game played on Lichess. Black's king has just stepped into the corner on h8, where its own pawns on g7 and h7 box it in. Look along the back rank.

credit.authors: Lichess; the position is from a game played there

notes.text: The queen takes the rook on a8, and the capture gives check along the eighth rank. The king cannot move, so Black's only answer is to block on e8 with the other rook.
Take the rook that blocked. Now nothing stands between your queen and the king, and the king still has no square: the queen covers g8, and g7 and h7 hold its own pawns. Checkmate.

parts.title: The knight's mate
parts.keyIdea: A king hemmed in by its own pieces can be mated by a lone knight, because a knight's check cannot be blocked.
parts.text: From a game played on Lichess. Black has just taken your queen on f5. You have only a knight left to attack with, but look at how Black's own pieces crowd the king on h8.

credit.authors: Lichess; the position is from a game played there

notes.text: The knight jumps to f7 and checks the king. Every square next to the king holds a black piece, a knight's check cannot be blocked, and nothing can take the knight on f7. This is called a smothered mate.
